newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - March 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - March 19.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- Chinese Premier Li Peng and Vice-premier Zou Jiahua attended a ceremony in the Guangxi region to mark the completion of an 899 km railway from Nanning to Kunming.
- Jiang Zemin approves provisional regulation on appointment and removal of military officers at and above the regimental level.
CHINA SECURITIES
- China issues rules on financial management of the futures markets.
- China's insurance premium income totals 85 billion yuan in 1996, with life insurance accounting for 33 billion yuan of that total.
FINANCIAL NEWS
- The Shenzhen Securities Exchange names the top 10 brokerages in terms of turnover in 1996. Guangdong Guangfa Securities Co heads the list.
- The Agricultural Bank of China renames its affiliated trust firm as the China Great Wall Trust and Investment Co. The trust company had total assets of 3.155 billion yuan at end-1996.
- The Bank of China signs an agreement with the Shanghai government pledging $300 million in loans a year to the Pudong development zone to the year 2000.
ECONOMIC DAILY
- China National Petrochemical Corp (Sinopec) generates pre-tax profits of 31.28 million yuan in 1996, a rise of 7.5 percent.
ECONOMIC INFORMATION DAILY
- The Ministry of Electronics Industry predicts sales of personal computers to hit 8-10 million units in the year 2000.
CHINA DAILY
- China will spend 10 years making large and medium-sized cities able to withstand the impact of earthquakes measuring six on the Richter scale.
- A commentary says the U.S. military should withdraw from East Asia.
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH
- Vice-premier Jiang Chunyun tells national conference on forest fire prevention that more efforts needed to protect the country's forestry resources.
